characters.reading_note: ガク → がっ via 促音 before こ

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ガク + コウ → がっこう (final ク assimilates before コ)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Universal anchor — every learner knows this word. Useful as a classification confidence-builder.
entries.real_world_context: N/A — anchor example. But demonstrates 促音 pattern that recurs in many 音音 compounds.

characters.reading_note: サイ is the correct on reading here, not サツ. Most learners only know 殺=サツ.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 殺 as サイ is unexpected for most learners who default to サツ. Common in business/legal contexts.
entries.real_world_context: Financial discussions — '利益を相殺する' (offset profits). Mispronouncing this as そうさつ in a meeting is a visible stumble.
entries.trap_note: Learners who know 殺=サツ will read this as そうさつ. The サイ reading is specific to this compound and a few related words (相殺勘定 etc.).

characters.reading_note: スイ is the 呉音 (go-on) reading, rarely encountered outside this compound and 出納係.
トウ is the 唐音 (tō-on) reading. Very rare — mainly survives in this compound.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Both characters use archaic on readings that most learners have never encountered. Functionally irregular despite being technically 音音.
entries.real_world_context: Office administration — 出納帳 (cash book), 出納係 (cashier/treasurer). Appears on forms and in accounting contexts. Reading this wrong marks you as an outsider.
entries.trap_note: Almost everyone's first instinct is しゅつのう. Both characters use their rarest on readings. Knowing this is 音音 doesn't help you predict the reading — you simply have to know it. This is an honest example of where classification fails as a prediction tool.

characters.reading_note: ゼイ is a rare on reading for 説, essentially only surviving in this word.

entries.contested_note: Prescriptive ゆうぜい, variant ゆうせつ — Native speakers commonly err. (From DATA_SPEC.md §7.4; the source entry records no alternate reading.)
entries.difficulty_rationale: 説 as ゼイ is a fossil reading. Appears in news/politics enough that advanced learners encounter it.
entries.real_world_context: Political news — 選挙遊説 (campaign tour/stumping). Comes up during election seasons. Reading it as ゆうせつ is common and noticeable.
entries.trap_note: Even native speakers sometimes say ゆうせつ. NHK prescribes ゆうぜい. Useful example for the 'native speaker ≠ ground truth' principle — many natives get this wrong too.

characters.reading_note: Both チョウ and テン are on readings. チョウ is the prescriptive standard here.

entries.contested_note: Prescriptive ちょうふ, variant てんぷ — Both widely accepted. (From DATA_SPEC.md §7.4; the source entry records no alternate reading.)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Widely mispronounced as てんぷ even by native speakers. Contested reading makes it tricky for learners.
entries.real_world_context: Document handling — '写真を貼付してください' on application forms. Email attachments. Bureaucratic contexts where getting it right signals competence.
entries.trap_note: てんぷ is so widespread that many dictionaries now list it as an accepted variant. This is a live example of reading shift in progress. Advanced learners should know ちょうふ is prescriptive but てんぷ won't get them corrected in practice.

characters.reading_note: サッ is a variant on reading (promoted 促音 form).

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ソウ + ソク → さっそく (促音 assimilation)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Very common word. Most learners know the reading but may not think about why it's さっそく rather than そうそく.
entries.real_world_context: Business email opener — '早速ですが...' Extremely high frequency. Good for showing 促音 as systematic rather than random.
entries.trap_note: The interesting teaching point is *why* さっ and not そう. The 促音 pattern (final vowel drops, consonant doubles before ソ/サ/カ etc.) recurs across many 音音 compounds.

characters.reading_note: ケイ is the less common on reading. Most learners default to キョウ.
ダイ is the 呉音 reading. Uncommon — most contexts use ナイ.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Both characters use their less common on readings. きょうない is the intuitive guess and is wrong.
entries.real_world_context: Temple/shrine visits — 境内マップ, 境内禁煙. Tourist situations where you're reading signs aloud or discussing with companions.
entries.trap_note: きょうない sounds plausible and is a common misreading. The 呉音 readings (ケイ, ダイ) signal Buddhist/temple vocabulary — a useful pattern to internalize.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Universal anchor. Immediately recognizable seasonal vocabulary.
entries.real_world_context: Spring social plans — 花見に行こう. Cultural touchstone that every learner in Japan encounters.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Clean anchor. Also useful contrast — 山道 is やまみち but 国道 is こくどう (音音). Same 道 character, different reading based on partner.
entries.real_world_context: Hiking, driving directions, rural travel. Signage in mountainous areas.
entries.trap_note: Note that さんどう also exists as a reading (mountain path in Buddhist/literary contexts). Context disambiguates, but this is a good example of the same compound having different readings in different registers.

characters.reading_note: かみ → がみ via 連濁

entries.phonetic_change_detail: かみ → がみ (連濁 — voicing of initial consonant in second element)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Everyone knows this word. Teaching value is in recognizing the 連濁 pattern.
entries.real_world_context: Daily life. Also a classic false friend for Chinese speakers (手紙 means 'toilet paper' in Chinese).

characters.reading_note: こ is an older/compositional kun reading of 木, seen in 木立(こだち), 木漏れ日(こもれび).

entries.difficulty_rationale: 木 as こ (not き) catches learners off guard. Recognizing this compositional kun pattern is useful.
entries.real_world_context: Outdoor situations, literary contexts. '木陰で休もう' — resting in the shade of trees.
entries.trap_note: Learners may try きかげ. The こ reading of 木 appears in several nature compounds and is worth learning as a pattern: 木陰, 木立, 木漏れ日.

characters.reading_note: かたり → がたり via 連濁

entries.phonetic_change_detail: かたり → がたり (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Well-known word. Good for demonstrating 連濁 in 訓訓 compounds — the pattern is extremely productive.
entries.real_world_context: Book titles, media — 源氏物語, film/anime titles. High cultural frequency.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Easy anchor. Note that 親子丼 keeps this reading — useful real-world extension.
entries.real_world_context: Restaurants (親子丼), family situations, legal contexts (親子関係).
entries.trap_note: Contrast with 親子 しんし which doesn't exist — but 父子 is ふし (音音). Same semantic field, different reading patterns.

characters.reading_note: あま is the compositional form of あめ, used when 雨 is the first element in compounds.
と → ど via 連濁

entries.phonetic_change_detail: と → ど (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: 雨 as あま (not あめ) is the teaching point — compositional forms of kun readings are a systematic pattern.
entries.real_world_context: Housing/daily life — storm shutters. '雨戸を閉めて' during typhoon season.
entries.trap_note: The あめ→あま alternation is productive: 雨戸, 雨雲(あまぐも), 雨宿り(あまやどり). Teaching this as a pattern rather than exceptions is exactly the tool's value proposition.

characters.reading_note: たな → だな via 連濁

entries.phonetic_change_detail: たな → だな (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Clean anchor for 重箱読み. The pattern (Sino-Japanese concept + native Japanese object) is visible.
entries.real_world_context: Furniture shopping, organizing. Extremely common household word.

characters.reading_note: ところ → どころ via 連濁

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ところ → どころ (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Classic example. Also demonstrates the semantic pattern: abstract/formal first element + concrete/native second element.
entries.real_world_context: Real estate listings, daily life. '台所が広い' — kitchen is spacious.

characters.reading_note: くみ → ぐみ via 連濁

entries.phonetic_change_detail: くみ → ぐみ (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Very common word. Good example of productive 重箱 pattern in media vocabulary.
entries.real_world_context: TV, radio, podcast discussions. 'この番組は...' — high-frequency media vocabulary.

characters.reading_note: ま is the kun reading meaning 'room/space'

entries.difficulty_rationale: 間 as ま vs カン is a key disambiguation. The 'room' meaning triggers kun reading.
entries.real_world_context: Traditional houses, ryokan. '客間にお通しください.' Architecture and hospitality vocabulary.
entries.trap_note: The 間=ま (room) pattern extends to 茶間, 居間, 床の間. When 間 means 'room/space,' it's usually ま (kun). When it means 'interval/between,' it's usually カン (on). This semantic split is genuinely useful for prediction.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Interesting because 毎+time-word creates a mini-system: 毎朝(まいあさ), 毎晩(まいばん), 毎日(まいにち). Classification varies within the set.
entries.real_world_context: Daily routine discussions. '毎朝6時に起きる.'
entries.trap_note: 毎朝 is 重箱 (on+kun), but 毎日 is 音音 (マイ+ニチ), and 毎晩 is 音音 (マイ+バン). Same prefix, different classifications depending on whether the second element uses on or kun. Good drill material for showing classification isn't about the word — it's about each character's reading.

characters.reading_note: コン is the less common on reading (呉音). Most learners know only ケン.
たて → だて via 連濁

entries.phonetic_change_detail: たて → だて (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: 献 as コン is unexpected. Most learners try けんだて or けんりつ.
entries.real_world_context: Restaurants, meal planning. '本日の献立' — today's menu. Also school lunch menus, hospital meal plans.
entries.trap_note: This is a genuine stumbling block. The コン reading of 献 is basically only alive in this compound. Useful for teaching that some readings are 'fossil' readings — they survive in specific words even though they're not productive anymore.

characters.reading_note: ふち → ぶち via 連濁. ふち='edge/rim' is the relevant kun reading.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ふち → ぶち (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: 縁 as ふち (not えん) is the key. Learners who only know エン will misclassify this as 音音.
entries.real_world_context: Art galleries, home décor, framing shops. '額縁に入れてもらえますか.'
entries.trap_note: Learners often know 縁=エン (fate/connection) but not ふち (edge/border). Different meaning, different reading. This illustrates why you need to know *which* meaning is active, not just which character is present.

characters.reading_note: し is the on reading (シ). Learners sometimes think it's kun because しごと 'feels' native.
こと → ごと via 連濁

entries.phonetic_change_detail: こと → ごと (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Misclassification trap. The word feels entirely native/kun, but 仕 is using its on reading. Tests whether learners verify each character independently.
entries.real_world_context: Universal — work, occupation. '仕事は何ですか.'
entries.trap_note: This is a calibration entry. If a learner classifies this as 訓訓 'because it feels Japanese,' they're using intuition rather than analysis. The tool should catch this and reinforce the verify-each-character habit.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Clean anchor for 湯桶読み. Common word, unambiguous classification.
entries.real_world_context: Trade shows, retail, business — 見本市 (trade fair), 見本品 (sample product). '見本をお見せします.'

characters.reading_note: ゆう is kun. The on reading セキ is rare (七夕=たなばた is irregular, not a counter-example).

entries.difficulty_rationale: Learners who think ゆう is on (confusing it with 有, 友, 優 etc.) will misclassify this as 音音.
entries.real_world_context: Newspaper reading, convenience stores. Pair with 朝刊(ちょうかん, 音音) for a nice contrast drill.
entries.trap_note: 夕刊 is 湯桶 (kun+on) while 朝刊 is 音音 (チョウ+カン). Same structure, different classification — because 夕 uses kun while 朝 uses on. Excellent drill pair.

characters.reading_note: あま is the compositional kun form (same pattern as 雨戸).
Voiced from ク via sequential voicing (連濁-like but within on reading context).

entries.phonetic_change_detail: グ is technically the standard on reading (already voiced), but the voicing reinforces the compound boundary.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Tests the 雨=あま pattern from 雨戸 in a different classification context. Cross-references reinforce learning.
entries.real_world_context: Travel preparation, outdoor activities. '雨具を持っていったほうがいい.'
entries.trap_note: If a learner already learned あま from 雨戸 (kun_kun), encountering it here in a 湯桶 compound reinforces that あま is about the character (雨's compositional kun form), not about the compound type.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 身 as み vs シン is the decision point. Most learners handle this correctly by instinct but may not consciously classify it.
entries.real_world_context: ID documents, social register. '身分証明書をお持ちですか.' Official/bureaucratic situations.
entries.trap_note: 身分証明書 extends this — the full four-character compound is (湯桶)(音音)(音), showing how classification applies recursively to compound words built from sub-compounds.

characters.reading_note: ば is kun. Learners sometimes think ば is on because it's so common in compound-like words.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Surprising classification. Most learners use this word daily without realizing it's 湯桶読み. Good 'aha moment' entry.
entries.real_world_context: Ubiquitous — location, place. '場所はどこですか.'
entries.trap_note: 場 on reading is ジョウ (as in 入場, 場面). The short ば is kun. Many learners assume short, common readings must be on. This entry challenges that assumption directly.

characters.reading_note: けし is the 連用形 (stem form) of けす.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Tests recognition of verb stem forms as kun readings in compounds. The 連用形 pattern is productive.
entries.real_world_context: Post office, mail. '消印有効' on application deadlines. Matters when submitting documents by mail.
entries.trap_note: The 連用形+on pattern appears in many 湯桶 compounds: 消印, 割引(わりびき — though 引 as びき could be argued either way). Recognizing verb stems as kun elements is a transferable skill.

characters.reading_note: おと is NOT a standard reading of 大. This is a 熟字訓 — the reading applies to the whole compound, not individual characters.
な is NOT a standard reading of 人. Reading cannot be decomposed by character.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Framework-breaker. The four-category system cannot classify this. 熟字訓 is a whole-word reading that doesn't decompose.
entries.real_world_context: Ubiquitous — adult. '大人1枚' at ticket counters. Also read as たいじん or だいにん in classical/formal contexts.
entries.trap_note: This entry exists to honestly show where the framework fails. 大人=おとな cannot be predicted from readings of 大 or 人. The tool needs a 'this is 熟字訓, learn it as a unit' category. If the system only has four categories, it will mishandle a significant chunk of common vocabulary.

characters.reading_note: き is not a standard reading of 昨. This is 熟字訓.
のう is not a standard reading of 日. Reading is whole-word.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Another essential framework-breaker. Everyone knows this word, but it cannot be derived from character readings.
entries.real_world_context: Daily conversation. Also read as さくじつ (音音) in formal contexts — which IS classifiable. Good for showing that the same compound can have both a 熟字訓 and a regular reading.
entries.trap_note: 昨日 has two readings: きのう (熟字訓, conversational) and さくじつ (音音, formal/written). This dual-reading pattern also applies to 今日(きょう/こんにち) and 明日(あした/あす/みょうにち). The tool should handle these as multi-reading entries where one reading is classifiable and one isn't.

characters.reading_note: シ is the prescriptive on reading for legal contexts. セ is used in construction and increasingly in general use.

alternate_readings.context: Construction/engineering contexts (工事の施行). Also increasingly used for legal contexts despite しこう being prescriptive.
Buddhist term — giving alms, charitable works (施行する).

entries.contested_note: せこう (variant — widespread but prescriptively contested): Construction/engineering contexts (工事の施行). Also increasingly used for legal contexts despite しこう being prescriptive.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Actively contested reading. しこう is prescriptive for law, せこう has taken over in construction and is spreading. Learners encounter both and don't know which is 'right.'
entries.real_world_context: Legal/regulatory — '法律の施行日' (law's effective date). Construction — '工事を施行する.' Both are common in business contexts.
entries.trap_note: This is a live example of reading change in progress. NHK and legal dictionaries prescribe しこう for laws. Construction industry universally uses せこう. The semantic split (law=しこう, construction=せこう) is the practical answer, but even this is eroding. Excellent for the 'native speaker ≠ ground truth' principle.

characters.reading_note: In だいがえ reading, 替=かえ is kun, changing the classification entirely.

alternate_readings.context: Increasingly common in business and media. Changes the classification from 音音 to 重箱.

entries.contested_note: だいがえ (variant — widespread, originally non-standard): Increasingly common in business and media. Changes the classification from 音音 to 重箱.
entries.difficulty_rationale: The だいがえ variant is so widespread that learners hear both and question which is correct. Classification itself shifts depending on reading.
entries.real_world_context: Business — '代替案を出してください' (please propose an alternative). Tech — '代替テキスト' (alt text).
entries.trap_note: だいがえ likely spread because だいたい is homophonous with 大体 (roughly/generally). The disambiguation pressure is real. This is a great example for teaching that reading shifts sometimes have practical motivations, not just 'corruption.'

characters.reading_note: ハン, not ボン. Most learners default to ボン (as in 凡人=ぼんじん, 平凡=へいぼん).

entries.difficulty_rationale: 凡=ハン is counterintuitive. Most learners' entire experience with 凡 is ボン.
entries.real_world_context: Maps, charts, dictionaries, technical documents — the legend/key section. '凡例を参照してください.'
entries.trap_note: ぼんれい is the most common misreading. The ハン reading of 凡 is essentially a fossil surviving in this word and 凡庸(はんよう... wait, that's actually ぼんよう). Actually 凡例 is one of very few places ハン survives as a standard reading.

characters.reading_note: 綻 is not a 常用漢字. Learners may not know any reading for it.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Straightforward 音音 once you know 綻=タン. The difficulty is that 綻 is rare as an individual character. But the compound itself is high-frequency in news/business.
entries.real_world_context: Financial/business news — '経営破綻' (business failure/bankruptcy). '交渉が破綻した' (negotiations broke down).
entries.trap_note: The reading isn't surprising — the compound is just intimidating because 綻 looks unfamiliar. Good entry for building confidence: if you guess on readings for both characters, you'll get it right. The system works here.

characters.reading_note: 捗 was added to 常用漢字 in 2010. チョク is the standard on reading.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Very common in workplace Japanese but 捗 is still unfamiliar as a standalone character for many learners.
entries.real_world_context: Project management — '進捗状況を報告してください' (please report on progress). Daily standup meetings, status updates.
entries.trap_note: Sometimes written as 進歩(しんぽ) by mistake — different word, different meaning. 捗 was only added to 常用漢字 in 2010, so older learners may have been taught to avoid it.

characters.reading_note: 訃 essentially only appears in this compound. No kun reading.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 訃 is a single-compound character — it only lives in 訃報. But the reading is predictable if you try on readings.
entries.real_world_context: News, social media — '訃報が届いた' (news of a death arrived). Knowing how to read this matters in social/professional contexts where the topic is sensitive.
entries.trap_note: Good example of the system working as designed: an unfamiliar-looking compound that yields to straightforward on-reading decomposition. Confidence builder for tier 2.

characters.reading_note: ヤク → やっ via 促音 before カ
款 is uncommon standalone but reading is predictable.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ヤク + カン → やっかん (促音: final ク assimilates before カ)
entries.difficulty_rationale: 促音 pattern is systematic. If learners know 学校(がっこう) pattern, they can predict this.
entries.real_world_context: Contracts, insurance, terms of service — '約款をご確認ください.' Banking, mobile phone contracts.
entries.trap_note: Good cross-reference with 学校 — same 促音 mechanism (ク before カ/コ). Building the 促音 pattern set is one of the module's highest-value contributions.

characters.reading_note: In よろん reading, 世=よ is kun.

alternate_readings.context: Originally よろん was the reading of 輿論 (different kanji). When 世論 replaced 輿論 after postwar kanji reform, the よろん reading transferred. Now both readings are standard for 世論.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Dual reading with different classification per reading. The historical reason is interesting but the practical issue is: both are correct, and the classification changes.
entries.real_world_context: News, politics — '世論調査' (public opinion poll). High frequency during elections.
entries.trap_note: せろん is 音音, よろん is 湯桶. Same kanji, different classification depending on reading. This is a rare case where the dual reading actually changes the compound's category. Historical footnote: よろん was originally 輿論 — the reading survived a kanji substitution.

characters.reading_note: ホウ → ぽう (半濁音化 after ン). Not 連濁 — this is a different phonetic process.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ホウ → ぽう (半濁音化: ハ行 after ン often becomes パ行). This is distinct from 連濁.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Commonly mispronounced as ねんぼう. The 半濁音化 pattern (ン + ハ行 → パ行) is systematic but less well-known than 連濁.
entries.real_world_context: Baseball/sports news, salary discussions — '年俸1億円' (annual salary of 100M yen). Also general employment contexts.
entries.trap_note: ねんぼう is a common error. The pattern ン + ホ → ポ also appears in 散歩(さんぽ), 乾杯(かんぱい). Teaching 半濁音化 as a systematic pattern alongside 連濁 and 促音 adds genuine predictive value.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 脆 is unfamiliar to many learners but the reading is straightforward on+on. IT security contexts make this increasingly common.
entries.real_world_context: IT/cybersecurity — '脆弱性が発見された' (vulnerability was discovered). Also general use — '脆弱な基盤' (fragile foundation).
entries.trap_note: Increasingly common due to cybersecurity news. Learners in tech environments hear this frequently. The on readings are regular — another confidence builder.

characters.reading_note: きっ is the 連用形 stem of きる with 促音.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: きり + て → きって (促音 in verb-stem compound)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Everyone knows the word. Teaching value is in recognizing verb-stem + noun as a productive 訓訓 pattern.
entries.real_world_context: Post office, convenience store. '82円切手を5枚ください.'
entries.trap_note: The verb-stem-as-first-element pattern: 切手, 割箸(わりばし), 焼肉(やきにく — though this is arguably 重箱 since 肉=ニク is on). Building this pattern set matters.

characters.reading_note: はな → ばな via 連濁

entries.phonetic_change_detail: はな → ばな (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Clean, predictable. Cross-references with 花見 — same 花 character, no 連濁 when first, 連濁 when second.
entries.real_world_context: Gardening, nature walks. '草花を育てる.'
entries.trap_note: Good 連濁 contrast pair: 花見(はなみ, no 連濁 — 花 is first) vs 草花(くさばな, 連濁 — 花 is second). 連濁 typically affects the second element, not the first.

characters.reading_note: ふ is a kun reading of 生 meaning 'growing/sprouting.' Very limited distribution — mainly this compound.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 生=ふ is a reading most learners don't know exists. 生 is famously the kanji with the most readings.
entries.real_world_context: Parks, sports, housing — '芝生に入らないでください' (keep off the grass). Signage at parks and sports grounds.
entries.trap_note: 生 reportedly has over 100 readings in names and compounds. ふ is one of the more obscure kun readings. This entry demonstrates that even 訓訓 classification can't help you predict the reading when one character has this many options.

characters.reading_note: ま as in 'time/effort' — same kun reading pattern as 客間 but different semantic domain.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Common word. Cross-references with 客間(きゃくま, 重箱) — same 間=ま, different classification because first character differs.
entries.real_world_context: Workplace — '手間がかかる' (takes time/effort). '手間を省く' (save effort). Very high frequency.
entries.trap_note: Builds the 間=ま pattern set: 手間(てま, 訓訓), 客間(きゃくま, 重箱), 居間(いま, 訓訓), 茶の間(ちゃのま, complex). The consistent ま reading regardless of partner kanji's reading type makes this a good prediction anchor.

characters.reading_note: わり is the 連用形 stem of わる.
はし → ばし via 連濁

entries.phonetic_change_detail: はし → ばし (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Common word. Verb-stem + noun pattern, same as 切手.
entries.real_world_context: Restaurants, convenience stores. '割箸はご入用ですか.' Daily food situations.
entries.trap_note: Verb-stem compound pattern: 割箸, 切手, 焼鳥(やきとり). Recognizing 連用形 as the first element in 訓訓 compounds is a high-value skill.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Parallel to 花見. Good for building the X+見 pattern set.
entries.real_world_context: Seasonal — autumn moon-viewing. Also 月見バーガー (McDonald's seasonal item), 月見うどん/そば (egg on noodles).
entries.trap_note: The 見=み pattern in nature-viewing compounds: 花見, 月見, 雪見(ゆきみ). Also 見=み in food: 月見うどん. Productive and predictable.

characters.reading_note: たち is the 連用形 stem of たつ.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Common word. Cross-references with 場所(ばしょ, 湯桶) — same 場=ば in different classification.
entries.real_world_context: Business, social situations — '相手の立場に立って考える' (think from the other person's position).
entries.trap_note: 場=ば appears in both 訓訓 (立場) and 湯桶 (場所). The character's reading stays the same — it's always ば(kun). The classification changes because the partner character's reading type changes. Good demonstration that classification is about the pair, not the individual character.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Common word. Extends the 場=ば cross-reference chain: 立場(訓訓), 場所(湯桶), 職場(重箱).
entries.real_world_context: Workplace — '職場環境を改善する' (improve the work environment). Daily use.
entries.trap_note: 場=ば now appears in three different classifications across the dataset: 立場(訓訓), 場所(湯桶), 職場(重箱). The character's reading is constant. Only the classification changes based on partner. This is the key insight the prediction chain drill should reinforce.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Fourth entry in the 場=ば chain. Now learners see the pattern clearly.
entries.real_world_context: Food, travel — '本場のナポリピザ' (authentic Neapolitan pizza). '本場の味' (the real/original flavor).
entries.trap_note: With 本棚(ほんだな) already in the dataset, 本場 extends the 本=ホン pattern too. Same first character, same reading, different second character. Both 重箱.

characters.reading_note: き is on (キ). Learners sometimes assume short common readings are kun — same trap as 場=ば.
もち is the 連用形 stem of もつ.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Like 仕事 and 場所, this is a word people use constantly without realizing its classification. 気=キ(on) surprises learners who assume it's kun because it's so common and short.
entries.real_world_context: Ubiquitous — '気持ちいい' (feels good), 'お気持ちだけで' (the thought alone is enough).
entries.trap_note: Builds the pattern: short, common-sounding readings aren't automatically kun. 気=キ(on), 仕=シ(on), 場=ば(kun but often assumed on). The drill should specifically target this assumption.

characters.reading_note: たか → だか via 連濁. The たか/だか reading meaning 'amount/value' is specifically the kun reading used in financial compounds.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: たか → だか (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: 高=だか (amount) is a distinct semantic use from 高=たかい (tall/expensive). Recognizing this financial meaning triggers the correct reading.
entries.real_world_context: Banking — '口座残高' (account balance). ATM screens, online banking, financial statements.
entries.trap_note: 高=だか in financial contexts is productive: 残高, 売上高(うりあげだか), 生産高(せいさんだか). It always means 'amount/quantity' rather than 'height/expense.' This semantic split reliably predicts the reading.

characters.reading_note: ガク (music) not ラク (pleasure). The 'music' on reading because backstage is originally a music/performance term.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 楽=ガク vs ラク choice depends on meaning (music vs pleasure). Semantic disambiguation in action.
entries.real_world_context: Theater, TV, events — '楽屋でお待ちください' (please wait backstage). Also figurative: '楽屋裏' (behind the scenes).
entries.trap_note: 楽 has two on readings with different meanings: ガク=music (音楽, 楽器, 楽屋), ラク=pleasure/ease (楽しい uses the kun, but 快楽=かいらく, 楽観=らっかん use this on). Knowing which meaning is active predicts the reading.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Clean example. Demonstrates the semantic heuristic: Sino-Japanese modifier (新=new) + native concrete noun (芽=sprout/bud).
entries.real_world_context: Gardening, cooking (tea), seasonal language. '新芽が出てきた' (new buds are coming out).
entries.trap_note: Cleanly illustrates the 重箱 semantic pattern: abstract Sino-Japanese adjective + concrete native noun. Compare: 新芽(しんめ, 重箱), 若葉(わかば, 訓訓). Both mean 'new growth' but 新 is on and 若 is kun.

characters.reading_note: In まいげつ reading, 月=ゲツ is on, making it 音音.

alternate_readings.context: More formal. Used in written/business contexts: '毎月の報告書' (monthly report).

entries.difficulty_rationale: Dual reading where classification changes. Extends the 毎X pattern from 毎朝. まいつき=重箱, まいげつ=音音.
entries.real_world_context: Scheduling, finance — '毎月25日が給料日' (payday is the 25th of every month).
entries.trap_note: The 毎X system is now well-populated: 毎朝(まいあさ, 重箱), 毎月(まいつき/まいげつ, 重箱 or 音音), 毎日(まいにち, 音音), 毎晩(まいばん, 音音), 毎年(まいとし/まいねん, 重箱 or 音音). Pattern: when the second character uses kun, it's 重箱. When on, it's 音音. 毎 itself is always マイ(on).

characters.reading_note: チャ is the 唐音 reading. 茶 has no standard kun reading — it was imported with the concept.
はたけ → ばたけ via 連濁. 畑 is a 国字 (Japanese-coined kanji) — it has no on reading.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: はたけ → ばたけ (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Interesting combination: 茶 has only on readings (imported concept), 畑 has only kun readings (国字). They can ONLY form a 重箱 compound.
entries.real_world_context: Travel (especially Shizuoka, Uji), food culture. '茶畑が広がっている.'
entries.trap_note: When one character has only on readings and the other has only kun readings, the classification is forced. 茶(on only) + 畑(kun only) = 重箱 by necessity. This structural constraint is a genuinely useful prediction tool.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Clean and common. Nice contrast with 見本(みほん, also 湯桶) — both have 本=ホン(on) as second element.
entries.real_world_context: Calligraphy, education, business — 'お手本を見せてください' (please show me an example/model).
entries.trap_note: 手本 and 見本 are near-synonyms and both 湯桶. The pattern kun-noun + 本(ホン) is productive: 手本, 見本, 絵本(えほん). Good mini-pattern.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Common word. Extends the 手=て(kun) + on pattern: 手本, 手帳, 手数(てすう).
entries.real_world_context: Stationery shops, organization — '手帳に書いておく' (write it down in my planner). Also 障害者手帳, お薬手帳 — official booklets.
entries.trap_note: 手 as the first element: 手本(てほん, 湯桶), 手帳(てちょう, 湯桶), 手紙(てがみ, 訓訓), 手間(てま, 訓訓). Same character, same reading, but classification depends entirely on the second character's reading type.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Third in the 手+on chain. Also extremely common in business (手数料).
entries.real_world_context: Business/banking — '手数料がかかります' (a fee will be charged). 'お手数ですが' (sorry for the trouble, but...) — essential business phrase.
entries.trap_note: お手数(おてすう/おてかず) in the polite phrase 'お手数ですが...' is ubiquitous in business email. Knowing the reading is essential for spoken professional Japanese.

characters.reading_note: え could be classified as either on (エ) or kun. Historical linguists debate this. Most modern references treat it as kun in this compound.

entries.difficulty_rationale: The 絵=え on/kun ambiguity is genuine. If え is on (エ), this would be 音音. If kun, it's 湯桶. This is an honest edge case.
entries.real_world_context: Bookstores, parenting, libraries — '絵本を読んであげる' (read a picture book aloud).
entries.trap_note: 絵 is a borderline case. エ appears in both on and kun reading lists depending on the dictionary. This is an honest example where classification becomes ambiguous not because of the compound but because of fundamental disagreement about the character's reading categorization. The tool should flag rather than force a classification.

characters.reading_note: シュク → じゅく (voicing after の). This is technically 連濁 applied to an on reading.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: シュク → じゅく (連濁 applied to on reading — unusual but attested pattern)
entries.difficulty_rationale: 連濁 normally affects kun readings. Here it affects an on reading, which challenges the usual rules. An honest complication.
entries.real_world_context: Travel, outdoor activities — '野宿する' (sleep rough/camp without shelter). Hiking contexts.
entries.trap_note: 連濁 on an on reading is unusual and complicates the otherwise clean rule that '連濁 = kun reading marker.' The tool should acknowledge this exists rather than pretend 連濁 only affects kun.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Useful contrast: 朝刊(ちょうかん, 音音) vs 毎朝(まいあさ, 重箱) vs 朝日(あさひ, 訓訓). Same 朝, three classifications.
entries.real_world_context: Brand names — 朝日新聞, アサヒビール. Also literal: '朝日が差す' (morning sun shines in).
entries.trap_note: 朝 is now in three classification contexts: 朝刊(チョウカン, 音音), 毎朝(まいあさ, 朝=あさ=kun → 重箱), 朝日(あさひ, 訓訓). The character's reading depends on whether the compound calls for on or kun — and that's contextual, not inherent.

characters.reading_note: はた is the clipped form of はたけ used in compounds. 畑 is a 国字 — no on reading.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 畑 has only kun readings (国字), so any compound with 畑 first is either 訓訓 or 湯桶 — never 音音 or 重箱. Structural constraint.
entries.real_world_context: Agriculture — '畑作農業' (dry-field farming). Contrast with 稲作(いなさく, 訓+on = 湯桶).
entries.trap_note: Pairs with 茶畑(ちゃばたけ, 重箱) — 畑 as second element is always kun. As first element too. A character that can only be kun constrains classification possibilities. This structural insight generalizes to other 国字.

characters.reading_note: きょ is not a standard reading of 今.
う is not a standard reading of 日.

alternate_readings.context: Formal/written — 'こんにちは' greeting derives from this. Also used in formal speech: '今日の会議' (today's meeting) can be either きょう or こんにち depending on register.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Universal word, completely undecomposable. Dual reading with こんにち(音音) makes it a perfect teaching pair.
entries.real_world_context: Daily life. '今日は何をする?' vs 'こんにちは' — different readings of the same kanji in universally common contexts.
entries.trap_note: Part of the time-word 熟字訓 trio: 昨日(きのう), 今日(きょう), 明日(あした/あす). All have both 熟字訓 and regular 音音 readings (さくじつ, こんにち, みょうにち). The register split is consistent: 熟字訓 = casual, 音音 = formal.

characters.reading_note: あし/あ is not a standard reading of 明.
た/す is not a standard reading of 日.

alternate_readings.context: Slightly more formal than あした but still 熟字訓. Common in business and news.
Formal/written. Business correspondence, announcements.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Three readings — two 熟字訓, one 音音. Completes the time-word trio.
entries.real_world_context: Daily life — 'また明日' (see you tomorrow). Business — '明日のミーティング' (tomorrow's meeting — あした or あす depending on formality).
entries.trap_note: 明日 has THREE standard readings with a register gradient: あした (casual) → あす (neutral/slightly formal) → みょうにち (formal/written). Only みょうにち is classifiable as 音音.

characters.reading_note: みや is not a standard reading of 土.
げ is not a standard reading of 産.

alternate_readings.context: Means 'local product' rather than 'souvenir/gift.' Different meaning from みやげ. '土産物(どさんぶつ)' = local product.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Dual reading where the meaning changes: みやげ=souvenir (熟字訓), どさん=local product (音音). Classification and semantics shift together.
entries.real_world_context: Travel — 'お土産を買ってきて' (bring back souvenirs). Gift culture, airports, station shops.
entries.trap_note: This is a case where the reading choice signals different meanings, not just different registers. みやげ ≠ どさん semantically. The classification framework correctly captures this: undecomposable reading = undecomposable meaning (熟字訓), regular reading = compositional meaning (音音).

characters.reading_note: しろ is not a standard reading of 素.
うと is not a standard reading of 人.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Completely undecomposable. Pairs with 玄人(くろうと). The しろ/くろ contrast suggests a folk etymology (white=amateur, black=pro) but the kanji don't support this.
entries.real_world_context: Business, conversation — '素人にはわかりにくい' (hard for a layperson to understand). '素人考えですが...' (this may be a layperson's thinking, but...).
entries.trap_note: The 素人/玄人 pair is a good teaching unit. Both are 熟字訓, both end in うと (not a reading of 人), and the しろ/くろ contrast creates a memorable mnemonic even though the etymology is debated.

characters.reading_note: くろ is not a standard reading of 玄 (though 玄 does mean 'dark/black' which may be the semantic link).
うと is not a standard reading of 人. Same non-reading as in 素人.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Pair with 素人. 玄 does mean 'dark/mysterious' which connects to くろ, but it's still 熟字訓 — the reading isn't compositional.
entries.real_world_context: Expertise discussions — '玄人好みの店' (a restaurant favored by connoisseurs). Less common than 素人 but important to recognize.
entries.trap_note: The 玄=dark → くろ=black semantic link is genuine — 玄 means 'dark/profound' (as in 玄関=entrance, originally 'dark gate'). But translating semantic connection into a reading rule would be overreach. This is 熟字訓: learn as a unit.

characters.reading_note: いな is not a standard reading of 田.
か is not a standard reading of 舎.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Common word, completely undecomposable. Most learners know the word but not that it's 熟字訓.
entries.real_world_context: Travel, family origins — '田舎に帰る' (go back to the countryside/hometown). Lifestyle discussions.

characters.reading_note: かわ is not a standard reading of 為.
せ is not a standard reading of 替.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Financial term that advanced learners in business need. Completely undecomposable.
entries.real_world_context: Finance — '為替レート' (exchange rate), '外国為替' (foreign exchange). Banking, news, international business.
entries.trap_note: Essential business vocabulary. The reading can't be guessed from the components. Also appears in 為替手形(かわせてがた, bill of exchange) where the 熟字訓 portion combines with regular readings.

characters.reading_note: つ is not a standard reading of 梅.
ゆ is not a standard reading of 雨.

alternate_readings.context: More technical/meteorological. '梅雨前線' (baiu front) always uses ばいう.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Seasonal vocabulary. Dual reading: つゆ (general, 熟字訓) vs ばいう (meteorological, 音音).
entries.real_world_context: Weather, seasonal life — '梅雨に入った' (rainy season has started). '梅雨明け' (end of rainy season). June-July conversation topic.
entries.trap_note: Like 土産, the reading choice correlates with context: つゆ for everyday conversation, ばいう for weather reports and technical discussion. In 梅雨前線(ばいうぜんせん), only ばいう is used — the compound context forces the 音音 reading.

characters.reading_note: な is not a standard reading of 雪.
だれ is not a standard reading of 崩.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Nature/weather 熟字訓. The kanji make semantic sense (snow + collapse) but the reading is undecomposable.
entries.real_world_context: Ski resorts, mountain areas, disaster news — '雪崩注意報' (avalanche warning). Also figurative: '雪崩式に' (in an avalanche-like manner).
entries.trap_note: Part of the nature-disaster 熟字訓 cluster. The kanji are semantically transparent (you can guess the MEANING from the parts) but the READING is opaque. This distinction — transparent meaning + opaque reading — is characteristic of many 熟字訓.

characters.reading_note: ゆ could be linked to 湯(ゆ) semantically — 浴衣 was originally bathing clothing — but it's not a standard reading of 浴.
かた is not a standard reading of 衣.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Cultural vocabulary essential for life in Japan. Completely undecomposable.
entries.real_world_context: Summer festivals, ryokan, onsen — '浴衣を着て花火を見に行く' (go watch fireworks wearing a yukata). Tourist situations, shopping.
entries.trap_note: The etymology (湯帷子=ゆかたびら, bathing garment, shortened to ゆかた) explains the reading but doesn't help predict it. Good example for the 'etymological note enriches understanding but doesn't replace memorization' principle.

characters.reading_note: くだ is not a standard reading of 果.
もの is a standard kun reading — but this doesn't change the 熟字訓 classification because 果=くだ is non-standard.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Interesting case: 物=もの IS a standard kun reading, but 果=くだ is not. When one character's reading is non-standard, the whole compound is 熟字訓 even if the other character's reading happens to be standard.
entries.real_world_context: Grocery shopping, restaurants — '果物売り場' (fruit section). Daily life.
entries.trap_note: Tests the classification rule: 熟字訓 = at least one character's reading can't be decomposed. Even though もの is a regular kun reading of 物, the compound is still 熟字訓 because くだ doesn't come from 果's reading list. You can't partially decompose.

characters.reading_note: なこ is not a standard reading of 仲 (though なか is — the extra う sound doesn't match).
うど is not a standard reading of 人. Same pattern as 素人/玄人 — 人 in 熟字訓 often takes non-standard readings.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Social/cultural vocabulary. 人 appears in multiple 熟字訓 with non-standard readings: 素人(うと), 玄人(うと), 仲人(うど), 大人(な).
entries.real_world_context: Weddings — '仲人を立てる' (have a matchmaker/go-between). Less common in modern weddings but still understood.
entries.trap_note: The 人 character in 熟字訓 is a useful pattern to flag: 大人(おとな), 素人(しろうと), 玄人(くろうと), 仲人(なこうど). In all cases 人 takes a non-standard reading. Recognizing X+人 as a potential 熟字訓 trigger is a learnable heuristic.

characters.reading_note: ホ → ぽ via 半濁音化 after ン.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ホ → ぽ (半濁音化: ン + ハ行 → パ行). Same pattern as 年俸(ねんぽう).
entries.difficulty_rationale: Everyone knows this word. Teaching value: 半濁音化 demonstration alongside 年俸 to build the pattern.
entries.real_world_context: Daily life — '散歩に行こう.' Universal vocabulary.
entries.trap_note: 半濁音化 pattern set: 散歩(さんぽ), 年俸(ねんぽう), 乾杯(かんぱい), 心配(しんぱい). All are ン + ハ行 → パ行. This is as systematic as 連濁 but less well-taught.

characters.reading_note: ハイ → ぱい via 半濁音化 after ン.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ハイ → ぱい (半濁音化). Third entry in the 半濁音化 pattern set.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Universal anchor word that happens to demonstrate 半濁音化.
entries.real_world_context: Daily life — '心配しないで' (don't worry). Extremely high frequency.
entries.trap_note: Good calibration entry: learners who know this word may never have noticed that ぱい is a modified form of ハイ. Making the unconscious pattern conscious is exactly the tool's purpose.

characters.reading_note: ハイ → ぱい via 半濁音化 after ン.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ハイ → ぱい (半濁音化). Fourth entry — pattern should be clearly visible now.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Social vocabulary everyone knows. Completes the 半濁音化 cluster with 散歩, 年俸, 心配.
entries.real_world_context: Social events — '乾杯!' (Cheers!). Nomikai, parties, celebrations.
entries.trap_note: Four entries now demonstrate ン+ハ行→パ行: 散歩, 年俸, 心配, 乾杯. The pattern is clearly systematic. A drill presenting all four together would crystallize the rule.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Fifth entry in the 場=ば chain. At this point the pattern should be fully internalized.
entries.real_world_context: Local government — '町役場' (town hall/office). Rural areas, administrative tasks.
entries.trap_note: 場=ば chain now has five entries across four classifications: 立場(訓訓), 場所(湯桶), 職場(重箱), 本場(重箱), 役場(重箱). The character is always ば. Classification is always determined by the partner.

characters.reading_note: やき is the 連用形 stem of やく.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends the verb-stem + noun pattern: 切手, 割箸, 焼鳥. Food vocabulary grounding.
entries.real_world_context: Izakaya, street food — 焼鳥屋 is everywhere. Menu reading.
entries.trap_note: The 焼+X pattern is productive in food vocabulary: 焼鳥, 焼肉(やきにく — note: 肉=ニク is on, making this 湯桶 not 訓訓), 焼魚(やきざかな, 訓訓). Good mini-set for showing how the same first element creates different classifications.

characters.reading_note: Same 連用形 stem as 焼鳥.
にく is on. 肉 has a kun reading (しし) but it's archaic.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Surprise classification. Most learners think of にく as 'just the word for meat' without registering it as an on reading. Pairs with 焼鳥(訓訓) to show same first element, different classification.
entries.real_world_context: Restaurants — 焼肉屋 is a staple. Menu reading, restaurant discussions.
entries.trap_note: 焼鳥(やきとり, 訓訓) vs 焼肉(やきにく, 湯桶): same 焼=やき, different classification because 鳥=とり is kun while 肉=にく is on. Perfect drill pair for food vocabulary.

characters.reading_note: 晩 has no standard kun reading. This forces 音音.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 毎X system entry. 晩 is on-only, so this can only be 音音.
entries.real_world_context: Daily routine — '毎晩9時に寝る.'
entries.trap_note: 毎X system update: 毎日(まいにち, 音音), 毎晩(まいばん, 音音), 毎朝(まいあさ, 重箱), 毎月(まいつき/まいげつ, 重箱 or 音音), 毎年(まいとし/まいねん, 重箱 or 音音). The pattern is now clear: 毎 is always マイ(on). Classification depends entirely on whether the second character uses on or kun.

characters.reading_note: In まいねん, 年=ネン is on → 音音.

alternate_readings.context: More formal. Written/broadcast Japanese. '毎年恒例の' (annual/every year's).

entries.difficulty_rationale: Completes the 毎X system. Dual reading with classification shift, same pattern as 毎月.
entries.real_world_context: Seasonal/annual discussions — '毎年桜を見に行く' (go see cherry blossoms every year).
entries.trap_note: The 毎X system is now complete. The drill should present all five as a set and let the learner see that 毎 never changes — only the partner determines classification. Dual-reading entries (毎月, 毎年) show that the same compound can shift classification by shifting the second character's reading.

characters.reading_note: さかな → ざかな via 連濁.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: さかな → ざかな (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Completes the 焼X food trio: 焼鳥(訓訓), 焼肉(湯桶), 焼魚(訓訓). Same first element, three entries, two classifications.
entries.real_world_context: Restaurant menus, home cooking — '焼魚定食' (grilled fish set meal).
entries.trap_note: 焼X set complete: 焼鳥(やきとり, 訓訓), 焼肉(やきにく, 湯桶), 焼魚(やきざかな, 訓訓). The classification hinges on 鳥=とり(kun), 肉=にく(on), 魚=さかな(kun). The learner who sees all three together learns to check each second character independently rather than assuming a pattern from the first.

characters.reading_note: Wait — ウ is the ON reading of 雨. This makes the classification 音音, not 湯桶.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends the 雨 chain but with on reading ウ instead of kun あめ/あま. Shows the same character in a different reading mode.
entries.real_world_context: Weather reports — '雨量が多い' (heavy rainfall). Meteorological contexts.
entries.trap_note: 雨 chain update: 雨戸(あまど, 訓訓, あま=kun), 雨具(あまぐ, 湯桶, あま=kun), 雨量(うりょう, 音音, ウ=on). Same character, three compounds, both reading types. The partner character's formality/domain signals which: native concrete nouns (戸, 具) pull kun, Sino-Japanese technical terms (量) pull on.

characters.reading_note: ば is kun, not on. 場 on reading is ジョウ.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Sixth entry in the 場=ば chain. Also corrects my own error in the analysis document — I initially second-guessed myself on this classification. 場面 is 湯桶, not 音音, because 場=ば is kun.
entries.real_world_context: Film, theater, conversation — '印象的な場面' (impressive scene). Also business — '場面に応じて' (depending on the situation).
entries.trap_note: I caught myself making the exact error this tool is designed to prevent: I temporarily thought 場面 might be 音音 because ば 'sounds' like it could be on. It's not — 場 on reading is ジョウ. This entry is calibration for the 'short common readings aren't automatically on' pattern.

characters.reading_note: Now using the on reading ジョウ, contrasting with all previous 場=ば entries.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Common word that provides the critical contrast: 場=ジョウ(on) here vs 場=ば(kun) in every other 場 entry so far.
entries.real_world_context: Events, facilities — '入場料' (admission fee), '入場券' (admission ticket).
entries.trap_note: 場 chain now has the key contrast: 場=ば(kun) in 立場/場所/職場/本場/役場/場面 vs 場=ジョウ(on) in 入場. The on reading appears in formal/compound Sino-Japanese contexts: 入場, 退場, 会場, 工場. The kun reading appears when 場 combines with native Japanese elements. This semantic-formality split is a genuinely predictive heuristic.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Second 場=ジョウ entry. Reinforces that Sino-Japanese partner → on reading for 場.
entries.real_world_context: Events — '会場はどちらですか' (where is the venue?). Conferences, weddings, exhibitions.
entries.trap_note: 場=ジョウ cluster growing: 入場, 会場. Add 工場(こうじょう/こうば — dual reading!), 退場(たいじょう), 登場(とうじょう). The ジョウ reading is productive in formal/institutional compounds.

characters.reading_note: In こうば reading, 場=ば is kun → still 重箱 (工=コウ is always on). But classification of こうじょう is 音音.

alternate_readings.context: Smaller-scale, workshop-like facilities. 町工場(まちこうば) = small local factory. More informal/familiar register.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Dual reading where both readings are standard but carry different nuance AND different classification. こうじょう=音音 (large factory), こうば=重箱 (small workshop).
entries.real_world_context: Industry, manufacturing, tours — '工場見学' (factory tour, always こうじょう). '町工場' (small local factory, always こうば).
entries.trap_note: This is a prize entry for the 場 chain. Same kanji pair, two readings, two classifications, and a real semantic distinction. The learner gets to see that reading choice isn't arbitrary — it encodes meaning. Large/formal = こうじょう(音音), small/familiar = こうば(重箱).

characters.reading_note: に is the 連用形 stem of にる (to simmer/boil).

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends the verb-stem food compound pattern. Also starts a cooking-method+物 set.
entries.real_world_context: Menu reading — 煮物 is a standard category on Japanese menus and in home cooking. '今日の煮物は何?'
entries.trap_note: Cooking-method + 物 pattern: 煮物(にもの), 焼き物(やきもの), 揚げ物(あげもの), 漬物(つけもの). All 訓訓 with verb-stem first elements. Productive, predictable, and directly relevant to menu reading.

characters.reading_note: つけ is the 連用形 stem of つける.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Second in the cooking+物 set. Clean verb-stem pattern.
entries.real_world_context: Restaurants, izakaya, home cooking. '漬物の盛り合わせ' (assorted pickles).

characters.reading_note: あげ is the 連用形 stem of あげる.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Third in cooking+物 set. Pattern is now unmistakable.
entries.real_world_context: Menus — 揚げ物 is a standard menu category. '揚げ物は控えている' (I'm cutting back on fried food).
entries.trap_note: Note: sometimes written 揚物 without okurigana. The reading doesn't change but the visual presentation might throw off learners looking for the げ.

characters.reading_note: さし is the 連用形 stem of さす.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Universal food vocabulary. Verb-stem + body-part noun compound. Cross-references with 身分(みぶん, 湯桶) — same 身=み in different classification.
entries.real_world_context: Restaurants, supermarkets — '刺身の盛り合わせ' (assorted sashimi platter).
entries.trap_note: 身=み chain: 身分(みぶん, 湯桶), 刺身(さしみ, 訓訓). Same character, same reading, different classification based on partner.

characters.reading_note: くみ is the 連用形 stem of くむ.
たて is the 連用形 stem of たてる.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Double verb-stem compound. Both elements are 連用形. Common in manufacturing/instructions.
entries.real_world_context: IKEA furniture, manufacturing — '組立説明書' (assembly instructions). '組立が簡単' (easy to assemble).
entries.trap_note: Interesting structural type: verb-stem + verb-stem. Both elements are 連用形, producing a noun. 組立, 取引(とりひき), 受付(うけつけ), 申込(もうしこみ). This is a productive compound type that's always 訓訓.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Second verb+verb compound. High-frequency business vocabulary.
entries.real_world_context: Business — '取引先' (business partner/client), '取引条件' (terms of trade). Banking, commerce.
entries.trap_note: Note that 割引(わりびき) also contains 引=ひき→びき(連濁). Cross-reference opportunity.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Third verb+verb compound. Essential workplace vocabulary.
entries.real_world_context: Offices, hospitals, hotels — '受付は1階です' (reception is on the first floor). '受付時間' (reception hours). Signage everywhere.
entries.trap_note: 付=つけ(kun) here contrasts with 付=フ(on) in 貼付(ちょうふ). Same character, different reading depending on the compound's overall pattern.

characters.reading_note: もうし is the 連用形 stem of もうす.
込 is a 国字 — no on reading. Like 畑, this constrains classification.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Fourth verb+verb compound. 込 being a 国字 (kun only) is a structural insight.
entries.real_world_context: Forms, applications — '申込書' (application form), '申込締切' (application deadline). Administrative situations.
entries.trap_note: 込 is a 国字 with no on reading, like 畑. Any compound with 込 has that element locked to kun. 申込, 見込み(みこみ), 追い込み(おいこみ). Structural constraint = prediction tool.

characters.reading_note: チョウ is the prescriptive on reading here. ジュウ is increasingly accepted.

alternate_readings.context: Originally non-standard but now widely accepted. NHK permits both. Many younger speakers prefer じゅうふく.

entries.contested_note: じゅうふく (variant — increasingly accepted): Originally non-standard but now widely accepted. NHK permits both. Many younger speakers prefer じゅうふく.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Actively contested reading. ちょうふく is prescriptive, じゅうふく is dominant in spoken Japanese. Both are 音音 but with different on readings for 重.
entries.real_world_context: Office/IT — '重複しています' (there are duplicates). Data management, form filling.
entries.trap_note: Like 施行 and 代替, this is a live reading shift. Prescriptive ちょうふく vs popular じゅうふく. Unlike those cases, both readings are 音音 — the classification doesn't change, only which on reading of 重 is used. Useful for teaching that 'which on reading?' is a real problem even when classification is clear.

characters.reading_note: つづき is the 連用形 stem of つづく.
がら (pattern/nature) is a kun reading.

alternate_readings.context: Common in spoken Japanese. Technically a misreading that has become standard through widespread use.

entries.contested_note: ぞくがら (variant — widely used, originally non-standard): Common in spoken Japanese. Technically a misreading that has become standard through widespread use.
entries.difficulty_rationale: The 'correct' reading つづきがら is 訓訓. The widespread variant ぞくがら is 重箱 (on+kun). Classification changes with reading, and the prescriptive reading is less commonly heard.
entries.real_world_context: Official forms — '続柄' (relationship to head of household). Government paperwork, insurance forms.
entries.trap_note: An honest example where the 'wrong' reading has largely won. Most people say ぞくがら. Forms still sometimes have furigana showing つづきがら. Advanced learners should know both. Good 'native speaker ≠ ground truth' entry because even the 'ground truth' here is debatable.

characters.reading_note: ソン vs ゾン is contested. NHK permitted both since 2014.

alternate_readings.context: Dominant in spoken Japanese. The 連濁-like voicing of ソン→ゾン is widespread.
alternate_readings.source_status: variant — NHK changed to permit いぞん in 2014

entries.contested_note: いぞん (variant — NHK changed to permit いぞん in 2014): Dominant in spoken Japanese. The 連濁-like voicing of ソン→ゾン is widespread.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Live pronunciation shift with a specific date when NHK changed its guidance. Both readings are 音音.
entries.real_world_context: Health, psychology, tech — '依存症' (addiction), '依存関係' (dependency). Very common in modern Japanese.
entries.trap_note: NHK used to prescribe いそん exclusively. In 2014, they acknowledged いぞん as acceptable. This has a precise datestamp, making it a good concrete example for the 'readings shift over time' lesson. 存 voicing also appears in 存分(ぞんぶん) where ゾン is standard.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Formal vocabulary that appears in business documents. 漸 is unfamiliar to many learners but the on reading is regular.
entries.real_world_context: Business documents, formal writing — '漸次移行する' (transition gradually). Reports, policy documents.
entries.trap_note: Often confused with 暫時(ざんじ, temporarily) which uses different kanji. The 漸/暫 visual confusion is a separate issue but worth flagging.

characters.reading_note: あら is an older/literary kun reading form of 新. Shortened from あらた.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 新=あら is an uncommon kun form. Most learners know あたらしい and シン but not the compositional あら. Also provides contrast with 新芽(しんめ, 重箱) — same 新, different reading.
entries.real_world_context: News, mystery, military — '新手の詐欺' (a new type of scam). '新手が加わった' (fresh troops joined).
entries.trap_note: 新 reading contrast: 新芽(しんめ, 重箱 — 新=シン on) vs 新手(あらて, 訓訓 — 新=あら kun). Same character, different reading, different classification. The 'fresh/new' meaning is the same — it's the compound convention that determines on vs kun.

characters.reading_note: 連用形 of わる.
ひき → びき via 連濁.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ひき → びき (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Common word. Another verb+verb compound like 取引. Cross-references with 引=ひき/びき.
entries.real_world_context: Shopping — '割引価格' (discount price), '2割引' (20% off). Retail, travel bookings.
entries.trap_note: 引 appears in both 取引(とりひき, no 連濁) and 割引(わりびき, 連濁). Why does 連濁 apply in one but not the other? This is actually irregular — both are verb+verb compounds but 連濁 behaves inconsistently. Honest acknowledgment of where the rules get messy.

characters.reading_note: いけ is from いける (to arrange/display). One of 生's many kun readings.
はな → ばな via 連濁.

alternate_readings.context: Means 'fresh/living flowers' (as opposed to artificial). Different meaning from the art form いけばな.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: はな → ばな (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: 生=いけ is an unexpected kun reading. Also dual-reading with meaning split: いけばな (flower arranging art) vs せいか (fresh flowers).
entries.real_world_context: Cultural activities — '生花を習っている' (I'm learning flower arrangement). Also florist shops for せいか meaning.
entries.trap_note: 生 adds another reading to its already enormous list: 芝生(しばふ, 生=ふ), 生花(いけばな, 生=いけ). Both are unusual kun readings that only appear in specific compounds. 生 is the poster child for 'classification tells you on vs kun, but doesn't tell you WHICH kun.'

characters.reading_note: ショウ (not セイ) on reading here.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 生=ショウ (not セイ) is the tricky part. Extends the 生 cross-reference chain into on reading territory.
entries.real_world_context: Life planning, education — '生涯学習' (lifelong learning), '生涯年収' (lifetime earnings).
entries.trap_note: 生 chain growing: 芝生(ふ, kun), 生花(いけ, kun), 生涯(ショウ, on). Multiple on readings too: 生活(セイカツ) vs 生涯(ショウガイ). This character alone demonstrates why 'which reading?' is the hard problem, not 'on or kun?'

characters.reading_note: き means 'raw/undyed/natural' — specific semantic domain.
ジ is the 呉音 reading, used in 地=じ meaning 'texture/quality/ground.'

entries.difficulty_rationale: Fourth distinct 生 reading in the dataset. 生=き (raw/natural) is a specialized kun reading. 地=ジ (texture) vs チ (place) adds another layer.
entries.real_world_context: Fashion, baking, textiles — '生地がいい' (good fabric/material). 'ピザの生地' (pizza dough). Different domains, same compound.
entries.trap_note: 生 now has FOUR different readings across entries: ふ (芝生), いけ (生花), ショウ (生涯), き (生地). A fifth, なま, appears in 生ビール and is probably the most commonly known. This character is a one-kanji argument for why the tool needs more than just on/kun classification.

characters.reading_note: いち is the prescriptive on reading here.

alternate_readings.context: Widely used in spoken Japanese. 一=ひと is kun, making this a three-character mixed compound. Many prescriptivists consider this an error.

entries.contested_note: ひとだんらく (variant — widespread but contested): Widely used in spoken Japanese. 一=ひと is kun, making this a three-character mixed compound. Many prescriptivists consider this an error.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Three-character compound with a contested reading. Demonstrates that the framework extends to longer compounds but gets messier. Also a live prescription/usage split.
entries.real_world_context: Work/projects — '仕事が一段落した' (work has reached a stopping point). Very common in business conversation.
entries.trap_note: ひとだんらく is so common that many native speakers don't know it's contested. Prescriptive いちだんらく makes it pure 音音(音). ひとだんらく would be 湯桶+音 (kun+on+on). This three-character entry tests the framework's extensibility and shows a live native-speaker error pattern.

characters.reading_note: カン here — the 'interval/between' meaning. Contrasts with 間=ま (room/space) in 客間, 手間, etc.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends the 間 chain with the on reading カン. Clean contrast with 間=ま entries.
entries.real_world_context: Social distancing, spacing — '間隔を空けてください' (please leave space between). Also '時間間隔' (time interval).
entries.trap_note: 間 chain: ま(kun) in 客間/手間/居間 when meaning 'room/space'; カン(on) in 間隔/時間/空間 when meaning 'interval/between.' The semantic split → reading split is one of the most reliable prediction heuristics in the dataset.

characters.reading_note: い is from いる (to be/reside).
ま = room. Same pattern as 客間, 手間.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends the 間=ま(room) chain. Fourth entry confirming the semantic pattern.
entries.real_world_context: Home life, real estate — '居間が広い' (the living room is spacious). Housing listings.
entries.trap_note: 間=ま (room) set now: 客間(きゃくま, 重箱), 手間(てま, 訓訓), 居間(いま, 訓訓). The ま reading is stable across all when the meaning is 'room.' Compare 間隔(かんかく, 音音) where the meaning is 'interval' and the reading shifts to カン.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends both the 本=ホン chain (本棚, 本場) and the 物=もの chain (物語, 煮物, 漬物).
entries.real_world_context: Shopping, art, food — '本物のダイヤモンド' (real diamond). '本物の味' (authentic flavor). Antique/art authentication.
entries.trap_note: 本=ホン now appears in 本棚(重箱), 本場(重箱), 本物(重箱) — consistently 重箱 when paired with a native kun-reading noun. Also 手本(てほん, 湯桶), 見本(みほん, 湯桶), 絵本(えほん, 湯桶) — consistently 湯桶 when 本 is the second element with on reading ホン. The character's position in the compound predicts the classification pattern.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends the 手=て chain into more business vocabulary.
entries.real_world_context: Business, logistics, police — '手配する' (arrange/prepare), '指名手配' (wanted person). Travel planning, event management.
entries.trap_note: 手=て chain now: 手紙(訓訓), 手間(訓訓), 手本(湯桶), 手帳(湯桶), 手数(湯桶), 手配(湯桶). Pattern visible: 手+kun-noun = 訓訓, 手+on-noun = 湯桶. Perfectly predictable.

characters.reading_note: シュ on reading — contrasts with every other 手 entry in the dataset.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Critical contrast entry. Every other 手 entry uses て(kun). This one uses シュ(on). Same character, finally in a different reading mode.
entries.real_world_context: Discussion, debate — '手段を選ばない' (will stop at nothing). Business strategy, ethics discussions.
entries.trap_note: 手 chain culmination: 手紙(て, 訓訓), 手間(て, 訓訓), 手本(て, 湯桶), 手帳(て, 湯桶), 手数(て, 湯桶), 手配(て, 湯桶), 手段(シュ, 音音). Six entries as て(kun), one as シュ(on). The on reading appears when the partner is also on (段=ダン). The formality heuristic applies: 手段 is more abstract/formal than 手紙 or 手帳.

characters.reading_note: チ here (not ジ). Contrasts with 生地(きじ) where 地=ジ.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Common address vocabulary. 地=チ vs ジ is a useful disambiguation: チ for 'ground/land' (番地, 土地, 地方), ジ for 'texture/quality/ground-base' (生地, 地元... wait, 地元=じもと uses ジ but means 'local'). The split isn't perfectly semantic.
entries.real_world_context: Addresses — '番地を教えてください.' Mail, registration, navigation.
entries.trap_note: 地 has two on readings: チ and ジ. Some patterns: 地震(じしん), 地元(じもと), 生地(きじ) use ジ. 番地(ばんち), 土地(とち), 地方(ちほう) use チ. The split is partly semantic, partly fossilized. Not perfectly predictable but worth noting.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends the 朝 chain. Colloquial/casual register. Both characters kun = 訓訓.
entries.real_world_context: Casual conversation — '朝飯前' (easy/before breakfast). 'まだ朝飯食べてない' (haven't eaten breakfast yet).
entries.trap_note: 朝 chain: 朝刊(チョウカン, 音音), 毎朝(まいあさ — 朝=あさ, 重箱), 朝日(あさひ, 訓訓), 朝飯(あさめし, 訓訓). When 朝 means 'morning' in casual/native contexts → あさ(kun). When it appears in formal/Sino-Japanese compounds → チョウ(on). 朝食(ちょうしょく, 音音) vs 朝飯(あさめし, 訓訓) — same meaning, different register, different classification.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Register pair with 朝飯. Hotel/formal contexts use ちょうしょく. Casual contexts use あさめし/あさごはん.
entries.real_world_context: Hotels — '朝食は何時からですか' (what time does breakfast start?). Formal dining situations.
entries.trap_note: 朝食(ちょうしょく, 音音, formal) vs 朝飯(あさめし, 訓訓, casual). The register-classification correlation is strong: formal Sino-Japanese → 音音, casual native Japanese → 訓訓. This pair makes the pattern explicit.

characters.reading_note: ゆう is KUN. Despite the formal compound, 夕 uses its kun reading. This makes the compound 湯桶, not 音音.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Breaks the register-classification pattern. 夕食 LOOKS like it should be 音音 (parallel to 朝食) but isn't because 夕=ゆう is kun. The formality heuristic fails here.
entries.real_world_context: Hotels, restaurants — '夕食は7時からです.' Same register as 朝食 but different classification.
entries.trap_note: This is a critical heuristic-breaker. 朝食(ちょうしょく, 音音) and 夕食(ゆうしょく, 湯桶) are used in identical contexts and feel equally formal, but have different classifications because 朝=チョウ(on) while 夕=ゆう(kun). The learner who assumes 'formal = 音音' gets burned here. Classification requires checking each character, not guessing from register.

characters.reading_note: kun, same as in 夕食 and 夕刊.
ハン(on) here, unlike 朝飯 where 飯=めし(kun).

entries.difficulty_rationale: Interesting: 夕飯 is less formal than 夕食 but 飯 uses its ON reading ハン, not kun めし. Register doesn't predict reading here either.
entries.real_world_context: Home/casual — '夕飯何にする?' (what shall we have for dinner?). Family conversation.
entries.trap_note: Meal compound matrix is now rich: 朝食(ちょうしょく, 音音), 朝飯(あさめし, 訓訓), 夕食(ゆうしょく, 湯桶), 夕飯(ゆうはん, 湯桶). 夕 is always ゆう(kun). But 飯 shifts: めし(kun) in casual 朝飯, ハン(on) in 夕飯 even though 夕飯 is also casual. The register-reading correlation is weaker than it first appears.

characters.reading_note: し is not a standard reading of 時.
ぐれ is not a standard reading of 雨.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Nature/weather 熟字訓. Extends the cluster: 梅雨, 雪崩, 時雨.
entries.real_world_context: Seasonal — late autumn/early winter intermittent rain. Literary/poetic. Also food: 牛肉時雨煮(ぎゅうにくしぐれに) — a dish name.
entries.trap_note: Also extends the 雨 chain — 雨 has now appeared as あめ, あま, ウ, and ぐれ(熟字訓). Four different surface forms for one character.

characters.reading_note: さ derives from さつき (旧暦五月). Not a standard reading of 五.
み is not a standard reading of 月.
だれ is not a standard reading of 雨.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Three-character 熟字訓. Literary/seasonal vocabulary. Completely undecomposable.
entries.real_world_context: Literary, seasonal — rainy season rain (originally lunar calendar fifth month). Also business jargon: '五月雨式に' (in a trickle/piecemeal). '五月雨式の報告' (reports coming in dribs and drabs).
entries.trap_note: The business usage 五月雨式 is surprisingly common — it's how people describe things arriving irregularly over time. An advanced learner working in a Japanese office will encounter this metaphorical use. The literal weather meaning is literary/poetic.

characters.reading_note: つい is not a standard reading of 一.
たち is not a standard reading of 日.

alternate_readings.context: Means 'one day' (duration). Different meaning from ついたち (first day of the month).
Business/formal — '一日付で' (effective the first of the month). Written formal contexts.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Three readings, two meanings, two classifications. Extends the calendar 熟字訓 domain (alongside 昨日/今日/明日).
entries.real_world_context: Calendar — '一日に会議があります' (there's a meeting on the first). Also '一日中' (all day long) uses いちにち. Context determines reading.
entries.trap_note: 一日 is a masterclass in dual-reading complexity: ついたち (first of month, 熟字訓), いちにち (one day, 音音), いっぴ (first of month, formal, 音音). The meaning determines the reading. Calendar dates are a whole sub-system of irregular readings that could be its own module.

characters.reading_note: は is not a standard reading of 二.
た is not a standard reading of 十.
ち is not a standard reading of 歳.

alternate_readings.context: Straightforward on-on reading. Used in formal/clinical contexts. '二十歳以上' in legal text could be either reading.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Three-character 熟字訓. Culturally important — coming of age. Completely undecomposable.
entries.real_world_context: Coming-of-age day, legal age, social situations — 'はたちになったら' (when you turn twenty). Celebrations, life milestones.
entries.trap_note: はたち derives from the old Japanese counting system (はた=20). This archaic number reading only survives in this word. Like ついたち, it's a calendar/number 熟字訓 — a domain where undecomposable readings cluster thickly.

characters.reading_note: コン is the 呉音. Most learners know only ケン.
リュウ is the 呉音. Most learners know only リツ.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Both characters use 呉音 readings. Buddhist/temple vocabulary. Same pattern as 境内 — 呉音 signals religious domain.
entries.real_world_context: Temple visits — 'この寺は800年前に建立された' (this temple was built 800 years ago). Sightseeing, history.
entries.trap_note: 建立 and 境内 both use 呉音 readings, and both are temple/religious vocabulary. This is a genuine pattern: Buddhist terminology often preserves 呉音 readings. If a learner encounters an unfamiliar compound in a temple context, trying 呉音 is a viable strategy.

characters.reading_note: こころ → ごころ via 連濁.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: こころ → ごころ (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends 物=もの chain. The 連濁 on こころ is an important pattern — it appears in 親心(おやごころ), 乙女心(おとめごころ), etc.
entries.real_world_context: Childhood memories — '物心がついた頃' (from the time I became aware/conscious). Memoir-style conversation.
entries.trap_note: 心=ごころ(連濁) is a productive pattern in X+心 compounds: 物心, 親心(おやごころ), 乙女心(おとめごころ). When 心 is the second element after a kun-reading noun, expect ごころ.

characters.reading_note: ブツ → ぶっ via 促音 before シ.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ブツ → ぶっ (促音 before シ).
entries.difficulty_rationale: Common word. Provides the 物=ブツ(on) contrast with 物=もの(kun) entries. Also 促音 pattern.
entries.real_world_context: Science, health — '物質の性質' (properties of a substance). '危険物質' (hazardous substance).
entries.trap_note: 物 chain: もの(kun) in 物語/煮物/本物/物心 vs ブツ(on) in 物質/物理(ぶつり)/人物(じんぶつ). Same formality split: concrete/everyday → もの, abstract/scientific → ブツ.

characters.reading_note: ね is the 連用形 stem of ねる.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Three-character compound: kun+kun+on. Doesn't fit neatly into the four categories. Demonstrates the framework's limit with longer compounds.
entries.real_world_context: Daily life — '朝寝坊した!' (I overslept!). Casual conversation.
entries.trap_note: Three-character compounds require recursive classification: 朝寝(あさね, 訓訓) + 坊(ボウ, on). The overall compound is kun+kun+on, which has no clean label in the four-category system. This reinforces the recommendation to focus the drill on two-character compounds.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Anchor for the abstract+abstract → 音音 heuristic. Two abstract Sino-Japanese concepts = on+on.
entries.real_world_context: Ubiquitous — '練習する' (to practice). Sports, music, language learning.
entries.trap_note: Included primarily to build the heuristic testing set. 練(refine) + 習(learn) = two abstract verbs of Chinese origin → 音音. Predicted by the semantic heuristic. Building enough anchor examples makes the heuristic testable.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Another abstract+abstract → 音音 anchor.
entries.real_world_context: Professional situations — '経験がある' (have experience). Résumés, interviews, business discussion.

characters.reading_note: タイ here, not ダイ (cf. 台所=だいどころ). The reading varies by compound.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Universal vocabulary. Teaching value: 台=タイ here vs ダイ in 台所. 風=フウ(on) vs かぜ/かざ(kun).
entries.real_world_context: Weather, seasonal — '台風が近づいている' (a typhoon is approaching). Essential Japan life vocabulary.
entries.trap_note: 風 reading contrast: 台風(フウ, on), 風邪(かぜ — 熟字訓), 追い風(おいかぜ, kun). Starts a 風 chain.

characters.reading_note: おい is the 連用形 stem of おう.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Clean verb-stem + noun pattern. Extends 風 chain with kun reading.
entries.real_world_context: Business/sports metaphor — '追い風が吹いている' (the wind is at our backs / conditions are favorable). Also literal sailing/cycling.
entries.trap_note: Contrast with 向かい風(むかいかぜ, headwind). Both verb-stem + 風(かぜ, kun) = 訓訓. The pattern is productive for wind-direction compounds.

characters.reading_note: かな is the compositional kun form of かね, used when 金 is the first element meaning 'metal.' Same あめ→あま pattern as 雨.

entries.difficulty_rationale: 金=かな (not かね or キン) is the compositional kun form. Same pattern as 雨=あま. Builds the compositional-kun-form concept.
entries.real_world_context: Hardware stores — '金物屋' (hardware store). Also kitchen/tools context.
entries.trap_note: Compositional kun forms: 雨→あま (雨戸, 雨具), 金→かな (金物, 金具). This is a systematic pattern where the standalone kun reading (あめ, かね) shortens or shifts when the character appears as the first element of a compound. Worth teaching as a transferable concept.

characters.reading_note: Same compositional kun form as 金物.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Same 金=かな pattern, different classification because 具=グ(on). Parallels 雨戸(訓訓) vs 雨具(湯桶).
entries.real_world_context: Hardware, construction, DIY — '金具を取り付ける' (attach hardware/fittings).
entries.trap_note: 金物(かなもの, 訓訓) vs 金具(かなぐ, 湯桶): same 金=かな, different classification. Perfectly mirrors 雨戸(あまど, 訓訓) vs 雨具(あまぐ, 湯桶). The compositional kun form stays constant — classification depends on the partner.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends 番 chain from 番組(重箱). 番号 is 音音 because 号=ゴウ(on).
entries.real_world_context: Ubiquitous — '電話番号' (phone number), '番号札' (number ticket). Daily administrative tasks.
entries.trap_note: 番 chain: 番組(ばんぐみ, 重箱) vs 番号(ばんごう, 音音) vs 番地(ばんち, 音音). 番=バン is always on. Classification depends on partner.

characters.reading_note: キン(on) here — contrasts with かな(kun) in 金物/金具.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends the 金 chain with the on reading. 金=キン in financial/abstract contexts, 金=かな in concrete/physical contexts.
entries.real_world_context: Business — '金額を確認してください' (please confirm the amount). Invoices, receipts, negotiations.
entries.trap_note: 金 chain: かな(kun, metal/physical) in 金物/金具 vs キン(on, money/abstract) in 金額/金融(きんゆう). Semantic split mirrors the on/kun split. Also extends 額 chain from 額縁(がくぶち, 重箱) — 額=ガク is always on.

characters.reading_note: ま is the prefix kun reading of 真 meaning 'true/peak/mid-.' Very productive.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Starts the 真+X intensifier pattern. 真=ま(kun) as a prefix is extremely productive.
entries.real_world_context: Seasonal — '真夏の暑さ' (midsummer heat). Weather discussions, travel planning.
entries.trap_note: 真+X set: 真夏(まなつ), 真冬(まふゆ), 真昼(まひる), 真夜中(まよなか), 真っ赤(まっか), 真っ青(まっさお). All use ま(kun). This prefix is always kun regardless of what follows — a reliable prediction anchor.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Second 真+season entry. Pattern confirmation.
entries.real_world_context: Seasonal — '真冬の寒さ' (midwinter cold).

characters.reading_note: ま → まっ via 促音 before カ.
Wait — is か on or kun here? Actually, か is NOT a standard reading of 赤. The standard on readings are セキ and シャク. This is arguably a special intensifier form.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ま + か → まっか (促音). But the か reading of 赤 is itself irregular — not standard on or kun.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Looks simple but is actually a classification problem. 赤=か doesn't fit neatly as on or kun. The 真っ+color pattern may be its own morphological category.
entries.real_world_context: Expressions — '真っ赤な嘘' (blatant lie), '顔が真っ赤' (face is bright red). Very common.
entries.trap_note: The 真っ+color pattern: 真っ赤(まっか), 真っ青(まっさお), 真っ白(まっしろ), 真っ黒(まっくろ). The color readings in these (か, さお, しろ, くろ) don't all match standard on/kun classifications. This pattern may resist clean four-category classification. Honest acknowledgment.

characters.reading_note: しろ IS a standard kun reading. Unlike 赤=か, this one classifies cleanly.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ま + しろ → まっしろ (促音)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Clean 訓訓 — 白=しろ is standard kun. Contrasts with 真っ赤 where the color reading is irregular.
entries.real_world_context: Daily life — '真っ白な雪' (pure white snow), '頭が真っ白になった' (my mind went blank).
entries.trap_note: 真っ白(しろ, clean kun) vs 真っ赤(か, irregular). Same 真っ+color pattern, but classification differs. The pattern's internal consistency is weaker than it first appears.

characters.reading_note: くろ IS standard kun. Classifies cleanly.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ま + くろ → まっくろ (促音)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Clean 訓訓. Third in 真っ+color set.
entries.real_world_context: Daily life — '日焼けで真っ黒' (dark from sunburn). '真っ黒な犬' (jet-black dog).

characters.reading_note: さお is NOT a standard reading of 青. Standard kun is あお. This is an archaic/dialectal form surviving in this compound.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: ま + さお → まっさお (促音)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Like 真っ赤, the color reading is non-standard. 青=さお is not in standard reading lists. Two of four 真っ+color entries resist classification.
entries.real_world_context: Expressions — '顔が真っ青' (face turned pale/white as a sheet). Shock, fear, illness contexts.
entries.trap_note: 真っ+color pattern summary: 真っ白(しろ, clean kun), 真っ黒(くろ, clean kun), 真っ赤(か, irregular), 真っ青(さお, irregular). 50% classifiable, 50% not. The pattern is learnable as a unit even though individual entries resist decomposition. Teaching recommendation: present as a set and acknowledge the irregularity rather than forcing classification.

characters.reading_note: Wait — くつ is the KUN reading of 靴. ぐつ is くつ with 連濁. So this is kun, not on. That makes this 訓訓, not 湯桶.

entries.phonetic_change_detail: くつ → ぐつ (連濁)
entries.difficulty_rationale: Clean 訓訓 with 連濁. Material+object pattern.
entries.real_world_context: Shopping, business dress — '革靴を買いに行く.' Professional attire discussions.
entries.trap_note: I initially misclassified this — mistaking ぐつ for an on reading when it's actually くつ(kun) with 連濁. Catching self-corrections like this during data entry demonstrates exactly the value of careful character-by-character verification. 靴 on reading is カ (as in 軍靴=ぐんか), not くつ.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Extends 額 chain: 額縁(がくぶち, 重箱), 金額(きんがく, 音音), 半額(はんがく, 音音). 額=ガク is always on.
entries.real_world_context: Shopping — '半額セール' (half-price sale). Retail, consumer situations.

characters.reading_note: On only — 茶 was imported with the concept.
On only.

entries.difficulty_rationale: Both characters on-only. Like 茶畑, 茶 forces on. Here, 碗 also has no kun, so classification is doubly constrained.
entries.real_world_context: Dining — '茶碗蒸し' (steamed egg custard), 'ご飯茶碗' (rice bowl). Daily food vocabulary.
